grade.first_issue: The assertion that repeatedly applying the neighborhoods contained in B forces B=(0,∞) is not explicitly justified.
grade.summary: The classification f(x)=x+c, c≥0, is correctly supported. The iteration identity, nonnegativity of g, equality of all positive defect values, and converse verification are sound. The sole material omission is a short local-to-global argument excluding coexistence of zero and positive defects.
strengths: Correctly derives g(f(y))=g(y), the iterate formula f^(n)(y)=y+ng(y), and hence g≥0.
Uses asymptotically close forward orbits to prove that all positive values of g coincide.
Correctly verifies every translation f(x)=x+c with c≥0.

errors.description: From the fact that each w∈B has (w−2√(wc),w+2√(wc))∩(0,∞)⊆B, the proof simply says iteration gives B=(0,∞). A rigorous completion should take the connected component of B containing w₀ and rule out finite positive endpoints using the same neighborhood property. This is short and direct, but it is load-bearing in eliminating the mixed case.
